Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to align on your latency SLOs (~p95 < 220ms for 512 tokens on customer-facing chat flows) and the privacy constraints for PHI adjacency. Per our discussion, I pulled together a short list of model/runtime candidates and the Redwood-verified performance snapshots so you can evaluate cost vs quality tradeoffs quickly. Attached: a prompt-set you can run locally (lightwell-eval-promptset-v1.jsonl) and our concise perf snapshot PDF.

High-level recommendations (shortlist):
- Llama-3-70B-chat (q4_0 / 8-bit): best quality if you need longer context consistency; expect lower TPS but superior instruction-following.
- Mistral-Instruct-30B (int8): strong quality/cost balance for conversational assistants; higher TPS on A100/MI300.
- Redw-Open-13B-8bit (Redwood-verified): fastest cost per token for 99% of your short turn use-cases; good candidate for initial pilot.

Redwood-verified snapshots (linked & attached): each snapshot includes per-model throughput (TPS measured at steady-state), and latency percentiles for typical 256/512/1024-token scenarios. Key callouts from the snapshots:
- Llama-3-70B-chat (hosted-dedicated, A100-80GB): p50=85ms, p95=210ms, p99=360ms (512 tokens); sustained TPS ~6.
- Mistral-Instruct-30B (dedicated, MI300): p50=70ms, p95=165ms, p99=310ms (512 tokens); sustained TPS ~12.
- Redw-Open-13B-8bit (hosted, T4/RTX equiv): p50=45ms, p95=110ms, p99=220ms (512 tokens); sustained TPS ~28.

Notes on quality/regression concerns:
- We recommend a prompt set with realistic user utterances (attached) and a small holdout set for regression checks.
- For quantized variants, expect small deltas in factuality/verbosity; we can run focused A/B evals against your sample dataset.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share a ~500–1,000 message anonymized sample (or a synthetic mirror) we can use to run a short confirmation pass.
2) Redwood runs a 48-hour benchmark with the three shortlisted configs and shares raw traces + summary.
3) We schedule a 30-min SRE call to discuss deployment surface (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and fallback routing policy.

Proposed dates: benchmark run Wed 6/16 — Thu 6/17, SRE call Fri 6/18. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and upload the traces to a shared Drive link.

Thanks,

>
> 2) Llama-3-70B-chat (q4): the 360ms p99 callout was from a dedicated A100-80GB pod with continuous-batching disabled (we run latency-first configs for chat). On Hosted multi-tenant instances p99 will be higher — ~1.2–1.6x depending on burst factor and instance sizing. If you require the lower p99 we recommend Redwood Dedicated or a pinned Hosted pool (reserved capacity).
>
> 3) Regression thresholds: for your use-case we typically define guardrails like:
>   - Hallucination (open-fact mismatch): <= 3% on targeted medical-QA prompts (we’ll benchmark vs your holdout).
>   - Utterance truncation/stop errors: <= 1% on 512-token samples.
>   - Response latency SLA: p95 <= 220ms for interactive flows (example target).
>
> Recommended canary plan:
> - Run a 48-hour head-to-head with synthetic mirror + small real holdout (500 messages): collect p50/p95/p99 traces, token costs, and a small human eval on ~150 critical prompts.
> - If quantized model selected, include a 1,000-example regression pass comparing quantized vs float baseline on QA accuracy and named-entity fidelity.
>
> Attachments: latency-traces-llama3-70b-sample.json (sample traces), redwood-perf-snapshot-20270614.pdf
